## Natural history notes

A small moth characterized by mottled brown to grayish wings with darker stained-looking patches and fine wavy markings that help it blend into bark, leaf litter, or dead vegetation. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats where suitable host plants and resting cover occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on plant material and serve as part of the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and other insect-eating animals.
